submission.justification: Sensor-T3 has the best resolution (about 6 um) but fails the hard efficiency requirement, with 82% after 2e16 neq/cm^2. Of the remaining two, Sensor-T1 has better resolution than Sensor-T2 (about 9 um against about 15 um). Both meet the efficiency requirement: T1 reaches 98.5% and T2 reaches 99.2%. I scanned T1 from 50 to 300 um, and its resolution is best near 150 um (8.77 um). Neighbouring thicknesses gave 9.18 um at 130 um and 8.91 um at 170 um, so the minimum is shallow and the differences between points of about 0.3 um may be within noise. The 150 um choice rests on unirradiated simulation.

requirements.evidence: T1 at 150 um gives 8.77 um. This is the best result among the technologies that pass the efficiency requirement. T2 at 100 um gave 14.8 um, and I did not scan T2 at other thicknesses.

The 2026 test-beam results show T1 at 98.5%. T3 is excluded at 82%. This efficiency was measured for the sensors tested, and I did not find a thickness-dependent efficiency figure for T1. Efficiency at 150 um is therefore an assumption.

requirements.requirement: One of the three listed technologies
